questions.question: What does a share of stock generally represent?
choices: A loan made by the shareholder to the government
An ownership interest in a company
A guaranteed deposit at a commercial bank
A fixed insurance payment

questions.question: What does an investor generally do when purchasing a newly issued bond?
choices: Lend money to the issuer
Buy voting control of every company
Purchase a checking account
Pay an insurance deductible

questions.question: What is a dividend?
choices: A fee charged for opening a deposit account
An automatic refund of a stock's purchase price
A required loan payment to a bank
A company's distribution of money or other value to shareholders

questions.question: What is diversification?
choices: Keeping all funds in one company
Borrowing to buy the most volatile asset
Spreading investments among different holdings
Selling every investment after one price change

questions.question: What is an investment portfolio?
choices: The collection of investments a person or organization holds
A guarantee against every market loss
A government list of approved purchase prices
A loan used only for buying insurance

questions.question: What is a capital gain?
choices: A charge for maintaining an investment account
A profit from selling an asset for more than its purchase cost
A required payment on a mortgage
A refund of previously paid insurance premiums

questions.question: What does an index fund generally seek to do?
choices: Guarantee a fixed return in every year
Hold only the manager's favorite single stock
Track the performance of a specified market index
Avoid holding any financial assets

questions.question: Why does diversification help manage investment risk?
choices: It prevents every investment from losing value
It guarantees that all holdings rise together
It removes the need to consider fees
It reduces dependence on the performance of a single holding

questions.question: How are expected return and risk generally related?
choices: Higher expected returns usually come with greater uncertainty or risk
Higher expected returns always mean guaranteed profits
The lowest-risk assets always earn the highest returns
Risk disappears when an asset becomes popular

questions.question: Why does an investor's time horizon matter?
choices: It guarantees that market prices rise before a deadline
It affects how much time is available to handle market fluctuations
It determines whether the investor must buy a single company
It makes all investment fees tax-free

questions.question: Why can investment fees have a large long-term effect?
choices: Fees automatically improve an investment's performance
Fees are charged only when an investor has no assets
Fees remove all risk of market losses
They reduce funds available to remain invested and grow

questions.question: Why is a company's past stock performance not a guarantee of future returns?
choices: Past prices are never recorded accurately
Stocks cannot change value after purchase
Business conditions and investor expectations can change
Every company is required to pay the same dividend

questions.question: What risk does a bondholder face if an issuer cannot meet its payment obligations?
choices: Default risk
Currency printing risk
Sales-tax risk
Deposit-withdrawal risk

questions.question: How does reinvesting earnings affect potential long-term growth?
choices: It guarantees that an investment never loses value
It allows earnings to contribute to future earnings
It removes the original principal from the account
It prevents investors from owning multiple assets

questions.question: Why should an investor be cautious about a promise of high returns with no risk?
choices: All legitimate investments must have identical prices
High returns are legally required on every investment
A guarantee of high returns proves the seller is licensed
Such a promise may hide risk or indicate fraud

questions.question: A stock bought for $40 is sold for $50, with no fees. What is the capital gain per share?
Which portfolio is less concentrated in one company?
choices: Holdings spread across many unrelated companies
Every dollar invested in one employer's stock
Several purchases of the same company's stock
One company's stock purchased through two brokers

questions.question: A person must pay tuition in two weeks using their saved money. What concern is especially relevant before putting it in a volatile stock?
choices: The company's past return determines the sale price in two weeks
Its market value could fall before the money is needed
A longer investment horizon removes the need to pay tuition on time
Owning a share provides the same withdrawal guarantee as an insured deposit

questions.question: An investment rises from $100 to $110, with no additional deposits, fees, or distributions. What is the percentage return?
Which action best supports evaluating an unfamiliar investment offer?
choices: Rely solely on testimonials in the advertisement
Assume a celebrity endorsement removes the risk
Send money before reading any disclosures
Examine credible disclosures, costs, risks, and the seller's credentials
